---
title: Specification
subtitle: Signed Instruction Blocks, version SIB/1 (draft)
aliases:
  - /spec/
---

A Signed Instruction Block proves who wrote an instruction to an AI agent and when. It does not
encode permissions, it does not vouch for the signer's intent, and it does not hide the
instruction. Humans write instructions in plain language; a verifier in the agent's harness labels
which text carries a valid signature; a permission classifier decides what the labelled text
allows. This specification covers the block, the verifier and what the verifier hands the
classifier. It does not cover the classifier's judgment.


## Scope

A conforming implementation guarantees three properties of a block whose status is `verified`:

1. **Authorship**: a named signer holding an enrolled key produced the signature.
2. **Integrity**: the instruction text, after the canonicalization rule the signer chose, is the
   text the signer signed.
3. **Validity window**: the block is being used within its issued and expiry times, by the
   audience it names.

Outside scope: the meaning of the instruction, whether the signer should have signed it, secrecy
of the instruction, compromise of the verifier host, and how signer identifiers map to people.


## Terminology

Block
: The unit of signed text: an instruction, three clear metadata lines and a detached signature,
  between marker lines. See [Block Format](format.qmd).

Instruction
: The plain text between the first two marker lines. The signature covers its canonical form.

Signer
: The human whose enrolled key produced the signature, identified by a stable string such as an
  email address, carried in the `iss` header field.

Key identifier
: The `kid` header field. Names one enrolled key of one signer, so a signer can hold several keys.

Audience
: The `aud` header field. Names the deployment or harness that may honor the block.

Canonicalization rule
: The named transformation applied to the instruction before signing and before verification.
  Carried in the `canon` header field. See [Canonicalization](canonicalization.qmd).

Verifier
: The deterministic component that extracts blocks, checks them and produces the manifest. It
  contains no language model.

Manifest
: The verifier's output: every block found, its status and its origin. See
  [Provenance Manifest](manifest.qmd).

Harness
: The runtime that executes an agent's tool calls and in which the verifier runs.

Classifier
: The component, usually a language model, that decides whether a proposed action is within the
  instructions the manifest shows to be human-signed. See [Classifier Policy](classifier-policy.qmd).


## Conformance Targets

Signer
: Software that produces blocks. It MUST implement [Block Format](format.qmd) and
  [Canonicalization](canonicalization.qmd), and it MUST show the signer the canonical instruction
  and the header terms before the key is used.

Verifier
: Software that checks blocks. It MUST implement [Canonicalization](canonicalization.qmd),
  [Verification](verification.qmd) and [Provenance Manifest](manifest.qmd), and it MUST pass every
  vector in [Conformance](conformance.qmd).

Harness
: A runtime that integrates a verifier. It MUST run the verifier before its permission decision
  on every tool call and MUST deliver the manifest as described in
  [Provenance Manifest](manifest.qmd) and [Classifier Policy](classifier-policy.qmd).


## Standards Used

- [RFC 7515](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7515) (JSON Web Signature) for the signature
  container and the `alg`, `kid` and `crit` header parameters.
- [RFC 7797](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7797) (JWS Unencoded Payload Option) for the
  detached, unencoded instruction (`b64: false`).
- [RFC 8785](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8785) (JSON Canonicalization Scheme) for header
  serialization.
- [RFC 3339](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3339) for timestamps, restricted to UTC with a `Z`
  suffix.
- [RFC 8032](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8032) (EdDSA) for the `EdDSA` algorithm, curve
  Ed25519.
- [WebAuthn Level 3](https://www.w3.org/TR/webauthn-3/) for the `ES256-webauthn` algorithm
  (reserved, Phase 2).
- [RFC 9580](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9580) section 7 (OpenPGP cleartext signatures) as
  prior art for the readable-text-plus-detached-signature layout.


## Versioning and Extension

- The `typ` header field carries the specification version. This document defines `SIB/1`.
- A verifier MUST reject a block whose `typ` it does not implement, with status `malformed`.
- A verifier MUST ignore header fields it does not know unless the field is listed in `crit`, in
  which case it MUST reject the block with status `malformed`.
- A verifier MUST reject an `alg` or a `canon` value it does not implement with status
  `malformed`. There is no `none` algorithm and no identity rule.
- A canonicalization rule, once published, MUST NOT change. A change is a new rule with a new
  version suffix, and both MAY be supported side by side.
- A new `alg`, `canon` value or header field is added by a new minor revision of this
  specification. A change to the marker lines, the signing input or the manifest schema is a new
  `typ`.
